explanations: The push channel wraps the gateway error with %v instead of %w. The text survives but the error chain is cut, so errors.Is(err, ErrUnsubscribed), errors.Is(err, ErrRateLimited) and errors.As with a *ProviderError all fail for push failures. A device token that the gateway reports as gone (410) is therefore treated as an ordinary failure instead of an opt-out, the dispatcher returns a joined error rather than ErrNoChannels, and Process answers Retry. The queue keeps redelivering a message that can never succeed. EmailChannel uses %w and does not have the problem.

B is right: classifyHTTP wraps a 400 in a *ProviderError, EmailChannel wraps it with %w, and Dispatch wraps the join with %w, so errors.As in Process finds it and the 4xx rule returns Drop. A ignores the 4xx rule. C is wrong because with no successful channel Dispatch returns an error. D is wrong because only a 429 is classified as ErrRateLimited.

D is right: the loop returns nil at the first channel that succeeds, and the failures slice is only used when no channel delivers. A and B assume failures are reported even after a later success. C is wrong because ErrNoChannels is only returned when no channel failed and none delivered.

C is right: ctx.Err() is checked at the top of each iteration, and its wrapped error matches context.Canceled in Process, which requeues the message. A and B contradict that branch. D is wrong because the loop returns before the push channel runs.
